clue.text: Type of roast with European's meticulous attention to presentation

parts.note: a spit roast is meat turned on a spit over a fire
with means and, joining two things
a European from Poland is Polish

explanation.surface: A recipe note pairs a spit roast with a continental chef's fussy plating.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit and polish is the idiom for scrupulous smartness and cleaning, as in a soldier's boot-shining routine.

clue.text: Did hesitation set back, if made earlier?

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the hesitation sound inside the word is turned round

parts.note: to do an act or a play is to perform it
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A performer wonders whether faltering delayed a scene prepared in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' reverses only the hesitation sound within the bigger word, leaving everything else in place; the surface reads like a question about stage fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Preformed means shaped or formed beforehand, so made in advance.

clue.text: Drier plaster can be applied with this right away

indicators.note: away means removed, so the right abbreviation is taken out

parts.words: plaster can be applied with this
parts.note: a plasterer spreads plaster with a flat-bladed trowel

explanation.surface: Dry plaster can be applied at once with this tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' looks like a comparative adjective; it is a noun, the thing that dries you. 'right away' looks like 'at once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a cloth used to dry yourself, making it a drier.

clue.text: Go after switching neon sign

indicators.note: after places the go word behind the rearranged letters
switching means changing round, so the letters of neon are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A neon sign flicks over and says go.
explanation.definitionFit: No Entry is the wording on a road or door sign forbidding access.

clue.text: Spots an indication of strong emotion after 22

definitions.meaning: small inflamed blemishes on the skin

definitions.text: an indication of strong emotion after 22
definitions.meaning: 22 is GOOSE, and goose ... rise on the skin with fear or excitement

explanation.walkthrough: Following 22 (GOOSE) makes goose pimples, the bumps on skin caused by cold or emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimples are spots; goose pimples are the raised skin that signals strong feeling.

clue.text: Perhaps ageless ethnological weave

indicators.note: weave means interlace, so the letters are worked together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A timeless textile studied by anthropologists, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'ethnological' minus those of 'age' ('less') are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer, a simple garment of woven cloth that never dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single piece of woven cloth worn round the hips, typical of many traditional cultures studied by ethnologists.

clue.text: After 22 marches to fight or flight

definitions.meaning: 22 is GOOSE: goose-... are the stiff-legged marching of soldiers going to war
a flight of stairs is a set of ...

explanation.walkthrough: Following 22 (GOOSE) gives goose steps, a military march. The surface plays on 'fight or flight', the body's alarm response.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps make up a flight of stairs; after GOOSE they are the stiff marching of parading troops.

clue.text: Done the crime?Now do the time!

definitions.text: Done the crime?Now do the time!

parts.words: Done the crime?Now do the time!
parts.note: a rhyming couplet that delivers a fitting punishment, a just reward in verse

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is itself a rhyme: a fitting reward for wrongdoing, put in poetic form.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic justice is the fitting punishment of a wrongdoer, and the rhyme makes the clue itself poetic.

clue.text: Fresh thyme's no use for feeling beat

indicators.note: to use something is to put it to work, here the letters of the preceding words worked into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe-s supplies a letter S here

explanation.surface: A cook complains that fresh thyme is useless for the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' is the anagram signal for the letters of 'Fresh thyme's no'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of rhythm is an instinctive feel for the beat in music or dance.

clue.text: Monumental shell, however exploded, results in defeat

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart and its pieces scattered, so these letters are rearranged
the shell of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of Monumental are taken

explanation.surface: A huge artillery shell bursts and the enemy is routed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shell' takes M and L from the ends of 'Monumental'; 'exploded' mixes them with HOWEVER. 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm an opponent is to crush or beat them completely, a synonym of defeat.

clue.text: Girl from Yorkshire needs …

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A northern lass needs something, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's first name.

clue.text: … the Yorkshire bread monster

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is clipped to t', written T
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: what a Yorkshire lass needs is a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously shortens 'the' to t' ('down t' pit').
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is an ugly giant or dwarf of Scandinavian folklore, a creature of the monster kind.

clue.text: TV shows and quizzes about fancy lace

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the quizzes go round the other letters

parts.note: quizzes are tests of knowledge

indicators.note: fancy as a verb of change: lace worked into a new, ornate arrangement

explanation.surface: Television programmes and quiz shows feature something about ornamental lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is the anagram signal, rearranging 'lace'; 'about' sends the quizzes word round it. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Telecasts are broadcasts by television, so programmes shown on air.

clue.text: CO2 ?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for a firm, and the 2 recalls the saying 'two's ..., three's a crowd'

explanation.walkthrough: CO2 looks like carbon dioxide; read it as CO (the business abbreviation) with the number two attached, as in the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people together make company in the proverb, and CO abbreviates a firm or business.

clue.text: Poses for the first time, quietly showing many talents

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the quiet letter replaces the time letter

parts.note: attitudes are poses struck by the body
T is the abbreviation for time, here the first one in the word
P stands for piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone striking poses for the first time quietly reveals a range of gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' (in place of) swaps P in for the first T of ATTITUDES; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitudes are natural abilities or talents.

clue.text: Sign so corporal is on 50% cut across the board

indicators.note: a cut applied across the board hits every item equally, so each of the four words loses half its letters

explanation.surface: A budget note: a corporal sees his pay halved in a cut applied to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first half of each word: S from 'so', CORP from 'corporal', I from 'is', O from 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Predator bombed Pearl Harbor, recognising no limits

indicators.note: bombed means blown to pieces, so these letters are rearranged
with no limits the outer letters of the word are dropped, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Japanese aircraft attacked Pearl Harbor without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no limits' strips H and R from 'Harbor', leaving ARBO; 'bombed' shuffles PEARL with it. 'recognising' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is an Arctic carnivore, a predator that hunts seals.

clue.text: Awake, went out rejuvenated

parts.note: someone awake is up
to go out with someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone up early went on a date and came back refreshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Updated means brought up to date, made new again, much as something rejuvenated is refreshed.

clue.text: Spitfire finally to fall in bank and dive in here

indicators.note: to fall in means to drop inside, so the letter goes into the other word

parts.note: to bank on something is to depend on it

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A Spitfire plane plunges into a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'Spitfire'; 'to fall in' drops it inside DEPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep end of a swimming pool is where you dive in.

clue.text: One who's learned from church type of power circles

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so the power word goes round the church

parts.note: solar power is energy taken from the sun

explanation.surface: An educated person draws on the church and a kind of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person, someone who has studied deeply.

clue.text: Dawn of the student union

parts.note: NUS (National Union of Students) rising, read upwards in a down entry, makes the first half

explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the UK's National Union of Students: in a down answer, NUS rising becomes SUN, then RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is the moment of dawn, when the sun comes up.

clue.text: Careful control in reporting what may be on line in Bangkok

indicators.note: reporting means the words are spoken, so we want something that sounds like the phrase

parts.words: what may be on line in Bangkok
parts.note: a railway line in Bangkok would carry a Thai train

explanation.surface: A railway in Bangkok is run with strict discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'Thai train' sounds like the phrase meaning firm restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a tight rein means holding the horse's reins short, an idiom for strict control.

clue.text: Bush transforming 14 into a 24

definitions.meaning: a shrub grown for its hairy green fruit
14 is COMPANY and 24 is CROWD: an unwanted third person turns a pair's 'company' into 'a crowd'

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'two's company, three's a crowd'; the extra person tagging along with a couple is the third wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooseberry is both a fruit bush and British slang for an unwanted third person with a couple.

clue.text: See 22
Top military support secret police

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
the SS were the Nazi security police

explanation.surface: A garment for the top military officer is backed by spooks.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for senior officers, as in 'top brass'.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass are the senior officers of the military, from the braid on their caps.

clue.text: C-word upset many people

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swearing upset a lot of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large gathering of people.

clue.text: Bitterness about extreme characters backing the wayward sovereign

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the assembled run is read in reverse
about means around, so the bitterness wraps round the extreme letters

parts.note: bile is a byword for bitterness
A and Z are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet

indicators.note: wayward means unruly and astray, so the letters of the word follow in a new order

explanation.surface: Resentment surrounds a wilful monarch who has lost her way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the alphabet's end letters inside the bitterness word; 'backing' reverses that whole run, and 'wayward' rearranges 'the' to finish the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is the name of English queens, each one a sovereign.

clue.text: Wardrobe assistants Bronwyn and Ffion open cupboards and drawers

definitions.meaning: two women with Welsh names who dress actors in a theatre's wardrobe department
a piece of furniture with open shelves above and cupboards and drawers below

explanation.walkthrough: Bronwyn and Ffion are typical Welsh women's names; a Welsh dresser is a traditional kitchen dresser with plate racks above a base of cupboards and drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh dresser is a sideboard with open shelving; people from Wales who dress actors are also Welsh dressers.
